questions.subject: RESEARCH_METHODS
questions.topic: The correlation a paired design assumes
questions.learningObjective: Explain why pairing requires positive correlation
questions.stem: Explain why a paired design only improves precision when before and after measurements are positively correlated.

answer.exemplar: A paired test removes between-subject variation only when the two measurements move together; if they are uncorrelated, pairing adds degrees-of-freedom cost without reducing variance, and if negatively correlated pairing would hurt precision.

questions.explanation: Pairing subtracts a subject effect that cancels when measurements agree; without positive correlation the cancellation fails and the paired test loses power.

questions.topic: The hypothesis a research question implies
questions.learningObjective: Explain the role of the null in testing
questions.stem: Explain why a hypothesis test needs a null hypothesis rather than testing the research claim directly.

answer.exemplar: A test needs a null because the sampling distribution is derived under a specific value, letting us compute how extreme the data would be if no effect existed; without that reference we cannot calibrate evidence.

questions.explanation: The null supplies a fixed reference value for the sampling distribution, enabling a p-value; testing the claim directly gives no calibration.
questions.hint: The null gives a reference value.
